topic: claude code action reviews pull requests
headline_marked: [[Claude Code Action]] reviews GitHub PRs without a server
headline: Claude Code Action reviews GitHub PRs without a server
summary: A new GitHub Action allows Claude to automatically review pull requests and respond to mentions in issues, streamlining developer workflows.
details: A new GitHub Action, `anthropics/claude-code-action`, enables developers to have Claude AI review every pull request and respond to @claude mentions in issues without needing to run their own server. This tool integrates directly with GitHub, picking up its mode from the workflow context.

The action can answer code-related questions, review pull requests, and even implement simple fixes. It operates on your GitHub runner, with API calls directed to a provider of your choice, including Anthropic direct, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry.

Setting up the action requires repository administrator privileges and involves installing the GitHub app and configuring necessary secrets. While the quickstart guide is tailored for direct Anthropic API users, documentation for cloud provider integrations is available in the repository.

For more advanced usage, a Solutions Guide within the repository offers complete examples. Developers can customize review patterns, limiting checks to critical folders or adding specific checklists to the prompt for more targeted feedback.
The project is actively maintained, with a migration guide available for users upgrading from older versions (v0.x) to the latest v1.0 inputs, which include prompt and claude_args.

topic: set up spacexai grok in google workspace
headline_marked: [[Grok AI]] now free in Google Workspace apps
headline: Grok AI now free in Google Workspace apps
summary: Elon Musk's chatbot can now be installed as a free add-on for Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides, offering AI assistance directly within your workflow.
details: SpaceXAI released a free Grok add-on for Google Workspace in July 2026, allowing users to integrate the chatbot directly into Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. The add-on is easily installed from the Google Workspace Marketplace and appears in a side panel, similar to Google's own Gemini.

Once installed, Grok can assist with various tasks within the Workspace apps. In Docs, it can transform rough notes into formatted drafts with headings and lists. In Slides, it can generate a presentation deck from an outline, adding slides that match the existing theme.

For Sheets, Grok can analyze selected ranges, provide answers with citations, highlight specific cells, write formulas, and insert charts. It can also rerun scenarios based on changing assumptions, with each modification recorded as an editable change.

While Grok is free to use, it requires extensive permissions. It asks for broad access to Google Docs and Slides files, and its Drive access is limited to files used with Grok. It also needs permission to connect to an external service, sending data to SpaceXAI.

This contrasts with Google's own Gemini chatbot, which is integrated into Workspace but requires a paid subscription for personal accounts or specific Workspace plans for business users. Grok's free availability makes it a notable alternative for users seeking AI assistance within their productivity suite.
